A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plugin research work. All 29 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original text-generation experiments on four datasets, ablations, distribution-shift analyses, and a human evaluation of 100 Adidas descriptions in Section 7 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, distribution-shift analyses, and human evaluation in Section 7 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same autoregressive reweighting model, normalized product of token probabilities, training objective, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use E2E NLG, Web NLG, CommonGen, and Adidas, including the same distribution-shift scenarios and product-description human evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Zeroshot, ICL-1, ICL-3, NewModel, WeightedComb, and TempNet in Tables 1–4; BDPL in Table 5; and LoRA in Table 7. v4 repairs TempNet and BDPL citations without adding or revising these evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, 40% hyper-validation allocation, seven generation metrics, greedy decoding, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged. BDPL retains the stated 75 API call budget.

E4.justification: Section 7.3 and Appendices C.5–C.6 retain the same base-model quality, reweighting depth, initialization, and architecture ablations. Distribution-shift analyses and Adidas case studies are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and means with standard deviations for the same experiments, including Tables 1–4 and 7. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedure changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative outcomes are unchanged throughout. For example, GPT2-XL Plugin BLEU on E2E NLG remains 0.2470 ± 0.009 in Table 1, and BDPL + Plugin BLEU remains 0.4527 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss-correction derivations, assumptions, and Theorem 1 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same lemmas and complete proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about logit-only adaptation, autoregressive label-noise correction, theoretical consistency, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning overfitting, context-sensitive reweighting, and distribution-shift adaptation are unchanged. The Impact Statement retains the limitations concerning complex reasoning and computational overhead.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameter searches, prompts, preprocessing, dataset counts, and efficiency information are unchanged. The embedded code and dataset links also retain the same destinations.

R1.justification: v4 supplies missing citations and bibliography entries for Diao et al. (2022), Liu et al. (2024), Qiu et al. (2024), Torroba-Hennigen et al. (2025), and Zhang et al. (2023). These resolve placeholders in existing discussions; the substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes resolve question-mark citation placeholders, restore missing citation years, and standardize bibliography venue wording. The prose, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: Citation repairs cause limited text and bibliography reflow, including one line of the Section 7 introduction moving onto page 6. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–7 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 resolves five missing references, including the sources for the already-evaluated TempNet and BDPL baselines, making attribution and source identification clearer. This is a limited documentation improvement; the scientific content, results, and appendices remain unchanged.
